note: Kiln epic B (t_fefe017fc2): the 16-item ask and the 12 tickets the owner planner returned for it. Items 13-16 have no ticket; 10-12 do. Used by the ask-items-uncovered plan check test.
ask:
Kiln epic B: beginner-facing output and polish (repo ~/work/app after epic A; gate `npm run verify`; Node built-ins only; no AI code in the default edition). Evidence from an independent hands-on QA pass and a spec audit against 7b6d8ba, quoted per item. One ticket per item, numbered acceptance, tests that fail without the change, "(operator)" for live checks; order tickets sharing a file serially. 1. C++ Outline symbols (deferred from 4b). ui/outline.js is a pure browser-side per-language regex outliner with no C++ rules. Add C++ (.cpp .cc .cxx .h .hpp .hh .hxx) with a small brace/scope stack: namespaces, classes/structs/unions, enums (incl enum class), free functions, methods (in-class and Cls::name out-of-class), ctors/dtors, template functions/classes; kinds namespace|class|struct|enum|function|method; names qualified by class (Dog::speak); source order. Handle Allman braces, ctor init lists, = default/= 0/= delete, prototype+definition (one entry, at the definition); ignore comments, strings, raw strings, #define lines; never if/for/while/switch/catch/lambdas. Goldens on the cpp-classes and cpp-constructors-raii Learn snippets and templates/hello-cpp*. (operator) Outline lists the Hello C++ symbols and click jumps. 2. clang-tidy output on the CLI. `kiln compile|run` prints raw clang-tidy stdout incl. system-header `note: frame #N` chains and `[1/2] Processing file /abs/path/main.cpp.` lines (multi-file and CMake). Print one line per in-project finding `file:line:col: warning : ` then `N clang-tidy findings` (`(M more not shown)` past 20); no frames, no progress lines; full raw output stays in the step log. Fixture tests. 3. Learner tidy profile (cpp/clang-tidy-profile.json disable list, with reasons in the note; update the pinned profile tests and golden Checks string): bugprone-exception-escape (fires on any main() using std::getline/iostream with a 7-frame trace, and differs between runs), performance-avoid-endl (fires on every Hello World line; Kiln's own endl-in-loop check covers the loop case), cppcoreguidelines-avoid-c-arrays, modernize-avoid-c-arrays and cppcoreguidelines-pro-bounds-constant-array-index (week-one array syntax). Keep clang-analyzer-*. 4. A definite bug found by clang-tidy is not "pass". `int a[3]={1,2,3}; int i=5; a[i]=7;` gives `warning: Out of bound access ... [clang-analyzer-security.ArrayBound]` then `[tidy:1] pass`. clang-analyzer-* findings are shown as likely bugs: the tidy step reads "found N likely bug(s)" (not "pass"; the run itself still passes), and the Helper shows them as 'Worth fixing', not 'Tip'. 5. No machine-readable fix-it lines in C++ output. Every diagnostic with a fix-it also prints `fix-it:"./main.cpp":{3:14-3:14}:";"` (from -fdiagnostics-parseable-fixits), CMake builds with absolute paths. Keep parsing them for fixes, but strip those lines from what the CLI, the Output panel and Problems show. 6. Sanitizer crashes summarised. A stack overflow prints AddressSanitizer:DEADLYSIGNAL plus 255 identical `#N in f(int) main.cpp:1` frames (~270 lines); a null write shows `#1 0x... ()` and a SUMMARY with the function missing, then `kiln: exit status 1`. Collapse repeated frames (`... f(int) at main.cpp:1, repeated 254 times`), drop unknown-module frames, and lead with one plain line: "Your program crashed: stack overflow - f() in main.cpp line 1 keeps calling itself" / "Your program crashed: it used a null pointer at main.cpp line 5"; the result line says crashed, not exit status 1. Keep the raw report in the step log. 7. Node runtime errors without internals. `console.log(totl)` shows the user's line then 7 `at Module._compile (node:internal/...)` lines and `Node.js v26.0.0`; the [check] step prints `at wrapSafe (node:internal/...)`. Drop node:internal frames and the version banner from what the user sees (keep in the step log). 8. Linker errors in plain words. Calling sub() declared in math.h but never defined shows `Undefined symbols for architecture arm64: "sub(int, int)", referenced from: _main in main.cpp.o ... clang++: error: linker command failed`. Add a Helper card and a CLI summary line: "sub(int, int) is declared but never defined - add its body to a .cpp file" (macOS ld and GNU ld 'undefined reference to' fixtures). 9. HTML/CSS compile runs and reports the checks. A page with href="styles.css" (file is style.css), src="mian.js", a missing img, `

...

`, inline `` and CSS `p { color: red` / `colr: blue` gives `kiln: compile pass` with no steps. Run the existing html/css kiln-checks as a visible compile step, add broken local link/src detection (missing file, with did-you-mean against existing files) and a syntax check of inline scripts; never print pass for a check that did not run. 10. Python output cleanup. Syntax errors print compileall noise (`*** Error compiling './main.py'...`, `Sorry: IndentationError: ...`): show only the plain SyntaxError block. Tracebacks read `File "/abs/.../py_typo/./main.py"`: show project-relative `main.py`. (Python exit codes are in epic A.) 11. CLI ergonomics: options must work after the path exactly as the usage text documents (`kiln run --entry other.cpp` and `--no-hold` currently fail with 'run takes one ' while `kiln run --entry other.cpp ` works); `kiln --help|-h|help` print usage, exit 0; an unknown option says `unknown option '--verbose'` (not 'run takes one '); a file instead of a folder says `kiln works on folders - try kiln compile py_ok`, a missing path says `no such folder: nope`; print the usage block only for real usage errors (not after --entry or platform errors); `kiln uninstall --check` on macOS says to move Kiln.app to the Trash; "Pick which file Run should start" names the flag (`choose one: kiln run py_two --entry a.py`). 12. Shipped templates are warning-clean under the default profile and tidy (greet_test.cpp modernize-raw-string-literal), and CMake configure chatter (`-- Detecting CXX compiler ABI info`...) and `make[2]: *** ... Error 1` lines are folded out of the user-facing output (kept in the step log). 13. projectsBase in the Settings dialog (SPEC-EASY §2 "configurable"): a text field wired through settingsField, using epic A's validation (refuses /, ~, system dirs) with the server's error shown inline. Changing projectsBase must refresh the project list at once (today the cached list keeps showing the old base's projects until a later rescan). 14. compile_commands.json for clangd (SPEC-CPP §1): also write it at the project root (or a .clangd CompilationDatabase pointing at .kiln-build/), never overwriting a user's own file; test that clangd-style lookup from the root finds it. 15. macOS menu shortcuts match the command registry (SPEC-DESKTOP §5): desktop/macos/main.swift gives Toggle Sidebar ⌘B while ui/commands.js binds Mod-B to compile; Close Tab ⌘W has no registry shortcut. Make the menu key equivalents match COMMAND_DEFS (drop ⌘B from Toggle Sidebar; give close-tab Mod-W) and extend test/macos.test.ts to compare menu key equivalents with registry shortcuts. 16. Docs match behaviour: SPEC.md §3/README:59 say FORCE_COLOR=0 but code deliberately removes it and sets NO_COLOR=1, PYTHON_COLORS=0 (Python 3.13 colours whenever FORCE_COLOR is set); README .kiln.json section omits the cpp {"recursive": true} key and the kind list omits web and folder-mode cpp/python/node; SPEC-CPP §1 says JSON diagnostics but code deliberately uses text + -fdiagnostics-parseable-fixits (Apple clang 16 rejects JSON). Update the docs; no code change.

tickets.title: C++ symbols in the Outline (ui/outline.js)
tickets.acceptance: 1. The hand-written expected lists for cpp-classes, cpp-constructors-raii, hello-cpp and hello-cpp-cmake match exactly (name, kind, line, order), and the diff shows the lists were not dumped from the new code. 2. Unit cases pass for Allman braces, init lists, =default/=0/=delete, prototype+definition as one entry at the definition, out-of-class Cls::name, templates, enum class, unions and nested namespaces. 3. No entries come from comments, strings, raw strings, #define, if/for/while/switch/catch or lambdas. 4. Outlines for other languages are unchanged (their existing tests pass). 5. The new tests fail without the change. 6. npm run verify passes. 7. (operator) In the app, the Outline for Hello C++ lists its symbols, and clicking one jumps to its line.
